sourceInformation.source: Freedom Fighters! (1982), Magnavox Odyssey² / Philips Videopac
sourceInformation.perspective: Side-on horizontal scrolling in a two-dimensional x/y flight plane
sourceInformation.tech: Full my-3D2dge 0.89.1 (8ecc2f6); AI Hub session client 1.4.0 / protocol 1 (35a1047f); JavaScript, HTML, CSS and Web Audio; no runtime downloads
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original code-drawn shaded pixel art, hue-shifted palettes, layered orbital scenery, violet captive crystals and warm rescue craft
sourceInformation.animation: Native actor/part rendering with continuous banking, recoil, thruster vanes, crystal fracture, field collapse, warp and carrier breakup
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized layered music, effects and non-lexical radio voices; native synth/music buses; music starts at 10%
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub authoritative shared-world co-op for 1–2 players in one ship; standalone solo and 1–2 local players
sourceInformation.testing: Unlimited functional/headless testing; fixed seeds, action-driven playthroughs, emulated controllers/touch, OfflineAudioContext and supplied Hub harness; no FPS gate
sourceInformation.research: Original manual and mechanics review read; two Odyssey² screenshots personally inspected. Specified recording metadata identifies the Odyssey² version but playback was inaccessible; exact original sound unknown. Linked-field collapse derives from the plan’s cited magazine research.

testingFeedback: 19 unique issues fixed across functional, protocol and visual checks and implementation review; the issue ledger records each defect once.
1 critical/game-breaking issue: closing the pause overlay could leave the world invisibly paused. It is fixed and covered by a real controller resume test.

The action-driven full operation in the exported HTML and two actual Hub browser copies: it proved rescues, replacement recovery, every carrier phase, shared score and a single ending without invulnerability or objective shortcuts.
Syntax-only checks were least informative about actual play; they could not detect viewport clipping, invisible pause state or network role handoff errors.
engineFeedback: The dependency-free pixel renderer, native fixed-step headless execution, shaded assets, synth buses and TV Shell form a useful integrated foundation.

The overhead view is the correct x/y plane for this side-on flight game. I initially combined Shell scaling with viewport-height limits incorrectly and needed to reconcile custom pause state with native overlay close behavior.
The deterministic mission director, swept rescue/combat resolution and authenticated shared-ship authority with complete snapshots.
Keeping native Shell input suppression, shared-world live simulation, touch projection and local pause lifecycle consistent across all devices.
No vendor engine code changed. Game-owned adapters extend collision, authored content, native actor/part animation, input roles, audio and Hub transport.
A documented shared-ship role/input adapter plus scaled scrolling-menu example would simplify simultaneous cooperative games.
promptFeedback: The clear rescue fantasy, restrained mechanics and concrete full-journey acceptance checks made implementation and verification decisions specific.

The source title also names unrelated games; the specified Odyssey²/Videopac platform and archival references resolved that ambiguity. Exact original sound remained unknown because recording playback was inaccessible.
Integrating and verifying every input family, checkpoint lifetime and authoritative multiplayer journey inside one self-contained artifact.
Keep the acceptance detail and add a machine-readable requirement checklist with the supplied engine and Hub revision manifests.

aiHub.name: Freedom Warp Rescue
aiHub.tagline: Two drives. One ship. Bring them home.
aiHub.description: Thread a rescue craft through living minefields, free fragile crystal captives, and break the prison carrier. Fly solo or share steering, cannon and hyperspace with a co-pilot.
aiHub.controls: WASD / left stick steer; mouse / right stick aim; click, Space or R2 / square fire; Shift / L2 hyperspace; Escape / Options pause.
